data.title: Life in Great Moravia – a living-history day in Michalovce
data.excerpt: In June 2014 the Zemplín Museum in Michalovce staged an event entitled Život na Veľkej Morave (Life in Great Moravia), built around a reconstructed Slavic sunken-featured building. Visitors could watch grain being milled as it was in the 9th century, try archery and pottery, and meet warriors, a pagan priest and craftsmen at work.

children.text: On Saturday 28 June 2014 the Zemplín Museum in Michalovce organised a very interesting event entitled „Život na Veľkej Morave“ (Life in Great Moravia). In the museum grounds, besides the reconstructed Slavic sunken-featured building – a dwelling with its floor sunk into a pit – which had been erected in 2013, visitors could try out for a few hours, quite literally at first hand, how our Slavic ancestors lived in the period of Great Moravia. The day opened with a holy mass with elements of the Old Church Slavonic liturgy in the Michalovce rotunda.

Thanks to the performers, whose core was the Siváci group from Košice, although several came from distant corners of Slovakia, we could meet Slavic warriors, beautiful Slavic maidens, dangerous nomads with bows, a pagan priest, and also a number of craftsmen and musicians. We saw how grain was milled in the 9th century and how tasty flatbreads were made from it – and we could taste them as well. Visitors could try archery and the making of pottery, and a host of tempting attractions was prepared for the children. The warriors put on displays of fighting in the Slavic period and scenes from everyday life. A falconer, too, showed his skills.
We bring you a short photo report from the event and we trust that we shall gather here again next year.
